study.question: Can tying only the common user/context/target part of the three auxiliary first tower projections, with within-forward reuse, remove redundant dense capacity and measured prediction work while preserving the current incumbent click AUC?
study.hypothesis: Observed limitation: g2-r0030-joint_marginal_reference has click AUC 0.6671249391761293, 315029 dense parameters, 320.4219s training, 25.4354s validation inference and 16.0636/16.1802ms model-batch p50/p95. Shrinking auxiliary adapters to 6 gives 0.6669390334913383 and 302117 dense parameters but 25.7205s inference and 16.1067ms p50: smaller parameter count did not give measured prediction savings. Click17/aux9 is worse (0.6667935091968438); embedding/scorer/tower reductions also previously lost quality. Source inspection finds the three auxiliary first tower affines independently transform the identical context/target prefix; only the corrected history suffix differs. A shared prefix map may retain sufficient auxiliary conditioning while removing two prefix matrices and two prefix evaluations. This is unverified: common context gradients can alter click embeddings, so an untouched click tower does not guarantee unchanged click quality. Ordinary weight tying and affine decomposition are inherited techniques, not a novelty claim.

nearest_work.difference: Archived standalone source matches initial candidate SHA256 61ed6da931b843da1cf07392c928b2ef92fc625a63bfb3b0abd07036599424de. Retain its summaries, adapters and towers except auxiliary first-layer common-input parameter sharing and execution. This is the closest local control.

Archived v4 primary text inspected at lines240-319 (especially266-277), plus abstract/introduction. Inherit unnormalized target-dependent local activation and Dice through the local implementation. DIN is a reference for pooling, not evidence for this auxiliary sharing choice or an exact four-task reproduction.

Pinned benchmark constructor/forward inspected at lines17-136: task-specific and shared task hubs, sequence projections and separate towers. Current proposal adds no hubs, gates, task tokens or sequence exchange; it ties only common-input submatrices of existing auxiliary first affine layers. Original INFNet paper is link-only, so no original-paper equivalence or priority claim.

Task-specific 14/10 residual adapters, zero final initialization and source-gradient restrictions

study.proposed_difference: For auxiliary first affine W[c,t,h]+b, compute A[c,t]+B_task h+b_task. Initialize all three A matrices from the already initialized cart prefix after the incumbent reset, with no random draws. Independent control clones A into three Parameters; tied cells register one shared Parameter object. Original pooled submatrices, biases and all remaining parameters retain their initialized values. shared_repeat evaluates A separately for each task; shared_reuse evaluates it once per forward and keeps all three gradient paths attached. Reference is byte-identical incumbent. This chain separates the bridge (split arithmetic plus common initialization), weight tying, and common-expression reuse. It does not establish superiority to every equally small model; a matched-parameter independent capacity control would be a reserved follow-up if promising.
predictions: Predeclare before host screening: candidate click AUC minus contemporaneous unchanged reference must be >= -0.0002 absolute, and >= imported entry g0-r0022-support_rotated_attached AUC minus0.0002. Current incumbent-based floor is0.6669249391761293; the contemporaneous reference governs if it changes. This is a practical screening tolerance, not statistical noninferiority evidence.

Cost utility requires fewer measured unique dense and total parameters, at least5% lower model-batch p50 and3% lower p95 than contemporaneous unchanged reference, at least2% lower full-validation inference seconds, with training wall time no more than5% worse under identical host conditions. Also report shared_reuse versus shared_repeat to isolate reuse. FLOPs and parameter savings alone are insufficient.

All four tasks remain trained and predicted; report all AUC/Logloss, auxiliary mean separately and fixed history slices with sample/positive/negative counts. Auxiliary guardrail: mean auxiliary AUC decrease <=0.005 and no individual auxiliary AUC decrease >0.01 relative to same-round reference. This is a guardrail, never the selection score.

Independent split and shared_repeat have identical initial predictions in exact arithmetic because common-prefix weights start equal. The former has independent updates; the latter sums auxiliary gradients into one Parameter. They need not match after training.

shared_repeat and shared_reuse have identical real-valued functions, initialization and unique parameter sets. Any BF16/gradient summation differences and cost noise must be measured. Reuse may lose to extra small-GEMM or slicing overhead, so no speed claim is presumed.

Expected parameter savings are 2*prefix_width*first_hidden; if actual feature widths are context192/target96/history112, total/dense/embedding counts become32034517/241301/31793216 versus32108245/315029/31793216. These dimensions are inferred from inherited topology/counts and require host confirmation; source derives widths from feature_map.
falsifiers: Click preservation failure or auxiliary guardrail failure rejects candidate utility even with lower latency.
No measured prediction-cost reduction rejects efficiency utility; fewer parameters or shorter training alone cannot rescue it.
If independent split already loses quality, sharing versus the original is not uniquely attributable; compare tied to independent and investigate the bridge before any mechanism claim.
A shared_reuse/shared_repeat quality discrepancy larger than rounding or seed variability requires diagnosis of graph, buffer or optimizer behavior; do not attribute it to shared capacity.

Missing mask/forward/backward checks, duplicate optimizer entries, incorrect unique parameter count, nonfinite outputs/loss, or a mutated frozen source/protocol are implementation failures, not scientific counterevidence.
alternative_explanations: Common prefix initialization differs from two original auxiliary towers; original-to-independent bridge combines initialization and BF16 arithmetic changes
Task-loss gradient summation, dense clipping and AdamW on tied parameters differ from independent adaptation; this is part of tying, not proof of latent representational redundancy
Shared context gradients can change click features despite preserving the click tower and blocked auxiliary item/scorer gradients
BF16 GEMM shape and addition order, backward accumulation order and optimizer traversal can change numerical trajectories
Runtime/load noise, GPU allocation and host loading overhead can hide or imitate savings
One fixed seed and repeated identical-seed receipts do not estimate independent seed uncertainty; repeated seeds alone do not isolate a mechanism
Auxiliary quality may trade against click; inherited auxiliary semantics are user/category/brand24h events, not advertisement conversion attribution
A smaller independent model could perform equally well; no equal-capacity allocation superiority claim without a new matched control
